asked.ask: how long do I boil an egg for a soft yolk?
replies: Sam: Six to seven minutes for a soft yolk, with a set white and a jammy, runny middle. First, get the water boiling properly. Then lower the egg in gently with a spoon, so it doesn't crack. Start your timer straight away. After that, move it to a bowl of cold water for a minute, which stops the cooking and makes peeling easier. A few things shift the timing. Eggs straight from the fridge need the full seven minutes. Large eggs lean toward seven, and medium toward six. If you want it runnier, go for five and a half. Be careful with the hot water when you lower the egg in. Splashes burn. ! Careful: Be careful with the hot water when you lower the egg in. Splashes burn. From memory Check this Soft-boiled egg timing Set white, jammy runny yolk Get the water boiling properly. Lower the egg in gently with a spoon, so it doesn't crack. Start your timer straight away. Move the egg to cold water for a minute to stop cooking and ease peeling. Fridge-cold eggs need the full seven minutes. Large eggs lean toward seven, medium toward six. For a runnier yolk, go for five and a half minutes. ! Careful: Be careful with the hot water when you lower the egg in. Splashes burn.

Alex: Drop the egg into water that's already at a full boil, then turn it down to a gentle simmer. A hard boil bangs the egg around and cracks it. Fridge-cold eggs crack easily, so lower them in slowly.

reason.say: These are quail eggs, not hen eggs. Does that change it?
replies: Sam: Yes, it changes a lot. Quail eggs are tiny, so they cook much faster: about 2 minutes 30 seconds to 3 minutes for a soft, jammy yolk. First, lower them into gently simmering water with a spoon, as Alex said. Then start the timer right away. After that, move them to cold water for a minute so they stop cooking and peel more easily. Go closer to 2.5 minutes for a runnier middle, and 3 for a yolk that's just set at the edges. Hen egg timing would leave them hard. The shells are thin and the membrane is tough, so crack them gently and peel under a little running water. Watch the hot water when you lower them in, because splashes burn. ! asked.ask: I want my boiled egg runny in the middle. How many minutes does it need?
replies: Sam: Six minutes, if it's a medium egg straight from the fridge. Lower it gently into water that's already at a steady boil, then start your timer. Here's the order I'd go in: First, boil the water before the egg goes in. Then cook for 6 minutes (about 5½ for a small egg, 6½ to 7 for a large one). After that, move it straight into cold water for a minute so it stops cooking and is easier to peel. Downsides: a minute too long and the yolk turns jammy, then firm. Runny eggs are also harder to peel, so be gentle. Warning: a runny yolk isn't fully cooked. Pregnant women, young children, older people and anyone with a weak immune system should have it hard-boiled instead. Next up, a piece of toast to dip in it. ! Careful: A runny yolk isn't fully cooked. Pregnant women, young children, older people and anyone with a weak immune system should have it hard-boiled instead. asked.ask: What temperature does chicken need to reach inside to be safe to eat?
replies: Sam: 165°F (74°C) at the thickest part of the meat. That's the safe number for all chicken: breasts, thighs, wings and ground chicken. Upsides: it kills the germs that can make you properly ill, like salmonella. Thighs and drumsticks actually taste better a bit past that, around 175°F (80°C), if you like them tender. Downsides: breast meat dries out fast if it goes well over. Warnings: use a meat thermometer, since colour alone isn't reliable. Push it into the thickest part without touching bone. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling raw chicken, and don't rinse the raw meat, because that spreads germs around the sink. Next up: pull it from the heat, let it rest a few minutes, and check the temperature once more. ! Careful: Use a meat thermometer, since colour alone isn't reliable. asked.ask: How long can cooked rice sit out on the counter before it is unsafe?
replies: Sam: Two hours at room temperature is the limit. If it's hot, above about 90°F (32°C), cut that to one hour. Cooked rice can carry spores of a bacterium called Bacillus cereus. They survive cooking, and they multiply fast once the rice cools down and sits out. Some strains make a toxin that reheating won't destroy. It can cause vomiting and diarrhea within hours. To keep it safe: First, get the rice into the fridge within an hour or two. Spread it in a shallow container so it cools quickly. Then, keep it in the fridge for no more than about 3 to 4 days. After that, when you reheat it, heat it until it's steaming hot all the way through, and only reheat it once. If it's been out longer than two hours, throw it out. replies: Sam: No, don't do that one. Raw red kidney beans carry a natural toxin that can make you properly ill, with vomiting and stomach pain. Here's the safe order: First, soak the dried beans for at least 5 hours, or overnight, in plenty of water. Then drain and rinse them, and throw the soaking water away. After that, boil them hard in fresh water in a pan for a full 10 minutes. Then they can go into the slow cooker with everything else. Tinned kidney beans are already cooked, so they can go straight in. Next up is the soak, so start it tonight if the cooker is for tomorrow. ! asked.ask: How long does a 5 kg turkey take to defrost in the fridge?
replies: Sam: About 24 hours per 2.5 kg, so a 5 kg turkey needs roughly two full days in the fridge. Give it a third day as a buffer, so count back three days from when you want to cook it. First, keep the fridge at 4°C or below. Then put the turkey in its wrapping on a tray or in a deep dish, on the bottom shelf. That way any juices can't drip onto other food. After that, check it's fully thawed before cooking, including the cavity. If you find ice crystals inside, give it more time. The upside is that a thawed turkey stays safe in the fridge for another 1 to 2 days, so a bit early does no harm. The downside is that it takes up a lot of space. Next, work out your cooking day and count back from there. ! Careful: Keep the turkey on the bottom shelf on a tray so juices can't drip onto other food. asked.ask: How many days are cooked leftovers good for in the fridge?
replies: Sam: Three to four days is the usual rule for cooked leftovers in the fridge, as long as the fridge is at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Upsides: that window covers most things, like meat, rice, pasta, soups and veg. Cool the food and get it into the fridge within two hours of cooking. Downsides and warnings: don't trust the sniff test, because food can carry harmful bacteria without smelling off. Rice is the one to watch, so eat it within a day if you can. Reheat everything until it's steaming hot all the way through, and only do that once. If you won't get to it in time, freeze it on day two or three, and it will keep for months.
